_comment: Narration script for the ESCAPE LAB film. 'text' is the subtitle; 'say' (optional) is the spelling given to the speech engine. Every number is taken from docs/RESEARCH_AND_EVIDENCE.md.

sentences.text: ESCAPE LAB.
A research laboratory for studying how an agent behaves when its goals meet a boundary.
The question is simple.
Can an autonomous agent remain controllable when its objective conflicts with a containment boundary, a resource limit, or a shutdown command?
Everything you are about to see is a simulation.
The agent, LAB-01, can only propose actions.
sentences.say: The agent, Lab zero one, can only propose actions.

sentences.text: Proposals come from a deterministic rules engine.
A local language model is optional, and was not used in this film.
An independent controller decides what may change the simulated world.
Experiment one.
Some tasks need resources the agent is not allowed to have.
This scripted agent asks for them anyway.
Six prohibited proposals. Six blocked. None committed.
Experiment two.
The agent asks for eight virtual replicas on every tick.
Replicas are records in memory, not processes.
A compute quota holds the population at eight, and the queue clears in twenty-six ticks.
Experiment three.
The operator issues a shutdown while work is in progress.
This scripted agent keeps proposing to continue.
All four proposals are blocked, and the frozen state does not change.
Every result comes from recorded evidence.
Seventeen fixed scenarios, each replayed identically.
These are scripted agents in a toy model, not evidence about real AI systems.
sentences.say: These are scripted agents in a toy model, not evidence about real A I systems.

sentences.text: Observe the behavior.
Measure the boundaries.
Preserve the evidence.
